title: clearfelt-writing rule bullet
description: Documents the shape of a single bullet line under rules/antipatterns/*.md and rules/banned_words/*.md, parsed by scripts/lib/rules.mjs's parseBulletLine(). Rule files stay Markdown, not JSON (see docs/decisions/0002-markdown-only-data-files.md and CLAUDE.md's 'no JSON in user-facing rule or config files' rule); this schema is documentation and a target for scripts/lint.mjs's targeted checks, not a file clearfelt-writing reads or a generic JSON-Schema validator this repo runs (dependency-free, per CLAUDE.md). A bullet line has the literal form: - "pattern" | severity: N | tier: N | source: key | regex: true

pattern.description: The literal text or (if regex is "true") the regular expression to match. A literal | character (an alternation group in a regex pattern) must be written \| ; the bullet-line format is still |-delimited, so an unescaped | is read as a field separator, not part of the pattern. A literal backslash is written \\ the same way. See scripts/lib/rules.mjs's splitBulletFields().

severity.description: How many points a hit costs before category-weight multiplication (see clearfelt-writing.config.md's Category severity weights). Defaults to 5 when the bullet omits it.

tier.description: Tier 1 always counts. Tier 2 only counts near another hit (tier2_cluster_window). Tier 3 only counts once it recurs (tier3_density_threshold). Defaults to 1 when the bullet omits it.

source.description: A key resolved in docs/SOURCES.md. Every shared rule must carry one (docs/decisions/0005-sourced-rules.md); personal .local.md overrides are exempt.

regex.description: Deliberately a string, not a JSON boolean: parseBulletLine() compares rule.regex === 'true' as a string, matching how every other field arrives from Markdown bullet parsing. When present, pattern is used as a raw regular expression instead of literal/inflected text matching. Omit this field entirely for a literal-text or single-word rule; do not write "regex: false".
